attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post. He is stating his view, not quoting Noble.

semantics.note: 'Has also meant' says the missing moat caused competitors to catch up, so 'causal' is right. The draft keeps the parts about Google and Anthropic catching up, some Chinese firms being close behind and cheaper, and the 'some Chinese companies' scope.

contract.note: The plain readings of 'caught up', 'not far behind' and 'ahead on price' are ordinary. The February window is a reasonable choice for a statement about the present. Requiring evidence of cause beyond rankings is demanding, since catch-up is itself a sign of no moat. Still, it matches the causal wording.

evidence.note: Independent, dated Feb 18. It puts Gemini 3.1 Pro first overall and shows GLM-5 and Kimi K2.5 cost about half as much to run. It also shows GPT-5.2 ahead on GDPval-AA. It speaks to who caught up and on price, not to the cause.

Independent, dated Feb 11. GLM-5, a Chinese model, ranks just behind Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.2 on GDPval-AA, at low per-token prices. This supports 'not far behind' and 'ahead on price', but not the cause.
Anthropic's own release post claiming top scores, including beating GPT-5.2 on GDPval-AA. This is a company disclosure, not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: Independent February evidence supports the observable parts. Gemini leads overall, Anthropic is competitive, and GLM-5 is close behind at lower cost. OpenAI still leads some tasks, which does not contradict 'caught up'. The contract also requires evidence that the missing moat caused the convergence. The packet admits it has none, and nothing contradicts the cause either. The support condition is not fully met and the contradiction condition is not met, so the outcome is unresolved.
